1.web: I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
1.asv: I say then, Did God cast off his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

2.web: God didn’t reject his people, which he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:
2.asv: God did not cast off his people which he foreknew. Or know ye not what the scripture saith of Elijah? how he pleadeth with God against Israel:

3.web: “Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have broken down your altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.”
3.asv: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, they have digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

4.web: But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
4.asv: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have left for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal.

5.web: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.
5.asv: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

6.web: And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.
6.asv: But if it is by grace, it is no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.

7.web: What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.
7.asv: What then? That which Israel seeketh for, that he obtained not; but the election obtained it, and the rest were hardened:

8.web: According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.”
8.asv: according as it is written, God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, unto this very day.

9.web: David says, “Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.
9.asv: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, And a stumblingblock, and a recompense unto them:

10.web: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Bow down their back always.”
10.asv: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, And bow thou down their back always.

11.web: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
11.asv: I say then, Did they stumble that they might fall? God forbid: but by their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

12.web: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fullness?
12.asv: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?

13.web: For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;
13.asv: But I speak to you that are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;

14.web: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.
14.asv: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy them that are my flesh, and may save some of them.

15.web: For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?
15.asv: For if the casting away of them is the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

16.web: If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.
16.asv: And if the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump: and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

17.web: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree;
17.asv: But if some of the branches were broken off, and thou, being a wild olive, wast grafted in among them, and didst become partaker with them of the root of the fatness of the olive tree;

18.web: don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.
18.asv: glory not over the branches: but if thou gloriest, it is not thou that bearest the root, but the root thee.

19.web: You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”
19.asv: Thou wilt say then, Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.

20.web: True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear;
20.asv: Well; by their unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by thy faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

21.web: for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
21.asv: for if God spared not the natural branches, neither will he spare thee.

22.web: See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
22.asv: Behold then the goodness and severity of God: toward them that fell, severity; but toward thee, God’s goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

23.web: They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
23.asv: And they also, if they continue not in their unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.

24.web: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?
24.asv: For if thou wast cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and wast grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree; how much more shall these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

25.web: For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,
25.asv: For I would not, brethren, have you ignorant of this mystery, lest ye be wise in your own conceits, that a hardening in part hath befallen Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in;

26.web: and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
26.asv: and so all Israel shall be saved: even as it is written, There shall come out of Zion the Deliverer; He shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

27.web: This is my covenant to them, when I will take away their sins.”
27.asv: And this is my covenant unto them, When I shall take away their sins.

28.web: Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.
28.asv: As touching the gospel, they are enemies for your sake: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.

29.web: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
29.asv: For the gifts and the calling of God are not repented of.

30.web: For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,
30.asv: For as ye in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,

31.web: even so these also have now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they may also obtain mercy.
31.asv: even so have these also now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they also may now obtain mercy.

32.web: For God has shut up all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.
32.asv: For God hath shut up all unto disobedience, that he might have mercy upon all.

33.web: Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!
33.asv: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!

34.web: “For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?”
34.asv: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?

35.web: “Or who has first given to him, and it will be repaid to him again?”
35.asv: or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?

36.web: For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.
36.asv: For of him, and through him, and unto him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever. Amen.
